title: Conservation and threats to biodiversity; Biodiversity and its measurement
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV08a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV07a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV07a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV08b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV07a#N.6a, EV08a#N.5, EV08b#N.8, EV07a#N.9a, EV08b#N.19.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Pollution
items.clue: Threat posed by pesticides and plastics

items.label: Genetic diversity
items.clue: The variety of alleles within one species

items.label: Species richness
items.clue: The number of different kinds of organism present

items.label: Keystone species
items.clue: An organism whose loss changes the whole community

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A rock pool holds limpets 8, barnacles 6, periwinkles 4 and sea anemones 2. Using d = N(N − 1) ÷ Σn(n − 1), what is the index of diversity?
Which factor is the overarching cause of the current biodiversity crisis, driving each of the specific causes?

options.text: Spread of cities over natural habitat
Natural climate shifts as in past eras

questions.explanation: Population growth drives hunting and over-exploitation, urbanisation, clearance for agriculture, pollution and the spread of invasive species.

questions.stem: A zoo has bred a rare antelope for 30 years from six founding animals. Which is the strongest scientific concern about releasing their descendants into the wild?

options.text: They are safe in the zoo, so release is not needed to secure the species.
Mutations will have given them alleles for zoo life, which they cannot lose again.
Being so numerous after 30 years, the herd must have regained the genetic diversity it started with.
Six founders carried few alleles, so the herd has little genetic variety to meet disease or change.

questions.explanation: Six founders carry few alleles, and inbreeding adds to the problem. Studbooks slow the loss, but cannot replace missing alleles.

questions.stem: Ecologists want to compare the species diversity of the plant communities in two meadows by calculating an index of diversity, N(N − 1) ÷ Σn(n − 1), for each. Which procedure is most appropriate?

options.text: List the different plant species found in each meadow, without counting the individuals of each.
Count the total number of plants in each meadow, without recording which species each belongs to.
Count the individuals of each species in several randomly placed quadrats of equal size in each meadow.
Count the individuals of each species in one quadrat placed in the middle of each meadow.

questions.stem: A rare orchid survives in one wild meadow. Its seeds are now stored in a seed bank, and plants grow in a botanic garden. The meadow is due to be ploughed. Orchid seeds need a particular soil fungus to germinate. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The orchid is now secure, because its seeds and living plants are held safely ex situ.
The meadow should be fenced and left alone, as keeping people out is all that a reserve needs.
The meadow should still be protected and managed, as ex situ stocks cannot replace the habitat or its fungus.
Seed banks can store any plant's seeds for ever, so the orchid can be regrown wherever it is wanted.
